sense: make or become twice as great

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, transitive; in the passive, to be doubled, grow twofold
evidence: Cic. Rep. 2.35: duplicāvit illum prīstinum patrum numerum
Verg. E. 2.67: sōl crēscentīs dēcēdēns duplicat umbrās
terms.comment: To double a number, a sum or a journey (duplicātō itinere, Caes. B.C. 3.76), and so to increase. In poetry and later prose also to bend double (duplicātō poplite, Verg. A. 12.927), and of words, to repeat (Cic. Or. 135; Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: the setting sun doubles the lengthening shadows

phrases.latin: prīncipiō duplicāvit illum prīstinum patrum numerum
phrases.english: first he doubled the old number of senators

sources: Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-ranieri-eclogae), checked against the editions named there.

Citations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j).
